What you are exploring

100% FICTIONAL

A small, readable demo district

Six subcatchments cover 18 ha. Eight nodes and seven circular pipes form a connected tree ending at one outfall. None of these objects come from your Bellinge project.

Surface accounting you can inspect

Baseline: roof area + 6 m road area + a known green-area false positive. Parking is initially omitted.

Refined area = roofs + revised roads + false positives + added parking − verified green correction

The green correction is only the known area incorrectly counted as impervious. It does not subtract all green land. Road, roof and parking areas are preclipped disjoint attributes. Street-width scaling assumes a constant length and no new overlap.

Complete land-cover map: replaces each catchment’s fraction using fictional full-coverage classification values. Parking, green corrections and width increments are disabled to prevent double counting.

Manual: replaces each fraction with your value, between 0 and 100%. Select a catchment in the inspector to edit it.

Geometry stays fixed

Areas, pipe lengths, widths and elevations are independent demo attributes. The SVG is schematic, not an area-measuring GIS map. A local DTM or revised street alignment requests regeneration; it cannot predict new boundaries or pipes here.

No hydraulic results are implied

There is no rainfall, infiltration model, SWMM engine, calibration or benchmark comparison connected. Discharge, flooding, surcharge, runoff reduction and model accuracy remain uncomputed.

Bring your project into the ecosystem

Custom project adapter available

Open Custom project to read your INP, matching GeoJSON and a surface CSV locally. Export a processing request for the downloadable Python runner; returned result packs can be inspected here.

  1. Prepare with HydroPrep / QGISClip terrain, streets, buildings, parking and green areas to the same study boundary. Check a suitable projected CRS, units, overlaps and coverage.
  2. Create a project packRetain the baseline .inp and the matching nodes, edges and subcatchment geometries. Record software versions and data sources.
  3. Apply the surface adapterUnion and intersect valid surface classes with subcatchments, calculate %Imperv and retain a change ledger. Custom parking and green masks need explicit adapter logic.
  4. Regenerate, validate and compareUse a new model version. Test network connectivity and elevations, then run identical rainfall before judging hydraulic differences.

Two practical integration paths

GIS path: prepare and audit surfaces in QGIS, then pass a project pack to the Python runner.

Python path: reproduce clipping and aggregation in an adapter, then inspect its outputs in QGIS. Both paths preserve the original model.

3. Local Python processing

A working file-based exchange. No automatic server connection is configured.

01

Export your request

Load your INP, optionally add prepared surface values, choose refinements and export smrf-processing-request.json. This file contains your model.

02

Run Python locally

Extract the runner ZIP. In its folder, run:

python smrf_runner.py --request "path/to/smrf-processing-request.json" --output "path/to/smrf-output"

Surface validation and model writing use the Python standard library. Optional SWMM execution requires your own engine and complete rainfall/input files.

03

Inspect the returned model

Import smrf-result.json. The site checks the baseline fingerprint, settings and proposed fractions before offering the returned refined.inp.

No runner result imported. Hydraulic simulation has not been executed by this site.
Supported files, CSV fields and processing boundaries

INP: reads subcatchments, junctions, outfalls, storage nodes, dividers and all five link types. SI and US units are normalized to hectares and metres. The original text is retained; the Python writer changes %Imperv in a separate output file.

GeoJSON: FeatureCollections with matching model IDs in properties.id or properties.name. Point, LineString, Polygon and MultiPolygon are supported for display. Importing GeoJSON replaces all INP map geometry to avoid mixing coordinate spaces. Prepare all GeoJSON files in the same CRS; features with unmatched IDs are not used.

Surface CSV: catchment_id,roof_ha,road_ha,parking_ha,green_correction_ha,baseline_road_width_m. Enter explicit zeroes where valid; blanks mean unavailable. Parking and green columns represent incremental additions and known errors. Width scaling assumes constant road length and no new overlap.

Pending capabilities: polygon clipping/union, raster processing, terrain redelineation and graph regeneration need a GIS adapter. Prepare surface totals in QGIS for this version. The optional engine hook runs locally; the hosted site does not execute Python or SWMM.

Session storage: custom models remain in memory until the page closes or you clear them. Export a request to keep the model and choices. Uploaded data are not added to the demo scenarios.
